newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CNI sees industry output up 5.0 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CNI sees industry output up 5.0 pct in 97.

text.p: Brazilian industrial output will grow between 4.5-5.0 percent in 1997 compared with expected growth of 1.5-2.0 percent in 1996, the National Industry Confederation said (CNI).
Jose Guilherme dos Reis, head of the CNI's economics department, said 1996 output appeared low because of the slow expansion of the economy in the first half of the year.
But he said that with falling interest rates and easier credit, combined with increasing investment levels in production, consumption would grow in 1997.
Dos Reis also said he expected consumer goods consumption to slow after high levels in 1996 while capital goods consumption should recover on the expectation of a bigger grains harvest.
He said consumption of domestically-produced capital goods plummeted in 1996 as they were substituted by imports.
